tex_content.html:
For every $C^1$ loop $c$ and $\zeta >0$, all sufficiently fine regular polygonal approximations $c_n$ have length within $\zeta $ of $L(c)$ and are joined to $c$ by a piecewise smooth annulus of area below $\zeta $. \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch Polygonal lengths converge to $L(c)$. For large $n$, $c_n$ is inside a normal neighborhood of $c$; the pointwise short geodesics between them sweep out annuli whose areas tend to zero.

□

\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Uniformity of the polygonal approximation over a compact family]
